title: One finite free source surjects after finitely many scalar extensions
statement: Let $A$ and $B_j$, $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ for $r\in\mathbb N$, be commutative rings in the same universe, let $f_j:A\to B_j$ be ring maps, and let $N$ be an $A$-module. Suppose each scalar extension $B_j\otimes_A N$ is a finitely generated $B_j$-module. There exist $k\in\mathbb N$ and an $A$-linear map $p:A^k\to N$ such that every scalar extension $B_j\otimes_A p$ is surjective. The family may be empty and its ring maps need not be flat or jointly faithful. No global finite generation of $N$ is concluded.

source.place: Tag 08EE, proof of lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent, choosing finite generators before attachment; generalized finite tensor-factor version; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08EE

proof.text: For each j choose finite generators of B_j tensor N. Mathlib TensorProduct.exists_finite_submodule_right_of_setFinite expands these into pure tensors and supplies a finite A-submodule S_j of N containing all required second factors. The B_j-linear image of B_j tensor S_j contains the generators, hence is all of B_j tensor N.

Take the finite sum T of the submodules S_j. Finite sums of finite modules are finite. Choose a finite free surjection A^k onto T using Module.Finite.exists_fin'. Compose with the inclusion T into N. For every j its scalar-extended inclusion is epic since it factors the scalar-extended inclusion of S_j. Scalar extension preserves epis as a left adjoint, so the composite remains epic. For r=0 the sum is zero.

theorem exists_finiteFree_scalar_surjections (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (r : ℕ) (B : Fin r → Type u) [∀ j, CommRing (B j)]
    (f : ∀ j, A →+* B j) (N : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (hfinite : ∀ j, Module.Finite (B j) ((extendScalars.{u, u, u} (f j)).obj N)) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ p : ModuleCat.of A (Fin k → A) ⟶ N,
      ∀ j, Epi ((extendScalars.{u, u, u} (f j)).map p)
